chapter: Los Angeles, Ellington and the recording scene
title: Barney Bigard and the credit for "Mood Indigo"
summary: They discuss how Irving Mills' name was on the song and Bigard only got credit and royalties after twenty years.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: No. And I understand now that Barney Bigard is reaping the rewards of "Mood Indigo."
Finally. Well, Barney got a little bit of it.
But it was twenty years before Barney got his name on..
Yeah. Irving Mills' name was on it and everybody except Barney, who actually wrote it.
Right. And it was the twenty years when it was the biggest hit that Barney didn't get any royalties.
But now it's a hit again, and Dottie is doing beautifully.
Absolutely. But at least Barney had the satisfaction of...
...of getting his name there and knowing that he finally got the credit he was supposed to have.
Not always on time, but yes.
No, not always on time. But you see, a lot of those things... Should we...
